propositions.text: validate_rows takes a list of row dicts and a schema mapping column names to type names in {int, str, bool}.
It returns a list of error strings, one per problem row, and an empty list when all rows are valid.
A missing column (a schema column key absent from the row) is one reportable problem.
A wrong type (the row value's type not matching the schema type name) is the other reportable problem.
At most one error is reported per row: the first problem found, scanning columns in schema order.
Errors are emitted in row order and rows numbered from zero by input index.
The missing-column message is exactly "row {i}: missing column '{col}'".
The wrong-type message is exactly "row {i}: column '{col}' expected {type}, got {actual}" where {actual} is the value's Python type name.
Type matching uses the value's actual runtime type, with bool and int kept distinct (a bool does not satisfy int and vice versa).
Columns present in a row but absent from the schema are ignored and are not errors.
An empty schema imposes no requirements, so every row passes.
